- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +5–10% below peak.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price falling from 75+), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is trending, model often lags; forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast using 5-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.33 spikes, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 10–15% for next 3–5 days.
